{{nihongo|'''Nomi Shrine'''|野見神社}} is a Shinto shrine in Nomi-cho, {{ill|Takatsuki|Q335423|qid=Q335423}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|Q122723|qid=Q122723}}. It is treated as a candidate for the Engishiki Nomi Shrine and was formerly ranked as a gosha. {{nihongo|'''Nomi Shrine'''|野見神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Settsu Province]].

== History ==
In the reign of {{ill|Emperor Uda|Q349267|qid=Q349267}} (late 9th century), an epidemic struck the area; after an oracle, the deity Gozu Tenno (identified with Susanoo) was enshrined and the epidemic subsided, leading to construction of a shrine.

When Takatsuki Castle was built, the shrine was revered as a castle guardian. In the 16th century, while {{ill|Justo Takayama|Q749873|qid=Q749873}} ruled Takatsuki, the shrine buildings inside the castle were destroyed and lands confiscated. In 1619, lord {{ill|Matsudaira Ienobu|Q5368670|qid=Q5368670}} rebuilt the shrine buildings.

After the 1868 separation of Shinto and Buddhism, the principal deity name was changed to Susanoo-no-Mikoto; Nomi no Sukune was additionally enshrined and the shrine renamed "Nomi Shrine." Because of this late renaming, some scholars argue the actual descendant of the Engishiki Nomi Shrine is the Nomi Shrine subsidiary of Kamigu Tenmangu in Takatsuki.

It was briefly ranked as prefectural shrine in 1871, then demoted to gosha in 1872 for the above reasons.

== Precinct ==
== Main buildings ==
* Honden - rebuilt in 1682
* Haiden - rebuilt in 2003
* Noh stage
* Shrine office

== Subsidiary and auxiliary shrines ==
* Nagai Shrine (founded 1793; associated with the Nagai lords of Takatsuki)
* Kojima Shrine
* Shisha Myojin (consolidation of four shrines in Taisho period)
* Takatsuki Ebisu Shrine (branch from Nishinomiya Shrine, founded 1956)
* Gokoku Shrine (for Takatsuki war dead)

== Annual events ==
* New Year's festival (Jan 1)
* Tondo fire rite (Jan 15)
* Setsubun festival (Feb 3)
* Baby crying sumo dedication (Apr 29)
* Summer purification (Jun 30)
* Autumn grand festival (second Monday of October)
* Niiname-sai (Nov 23)
* Year-end purification (Dec 31)

== Cultural properties ==
== Takatsuki City designated tangible cultural properties ==
* Nagai Shrine buildings (honden and haiden), with 4 munafuda and 1 Takatsuki Castle ema (designated June 14, 2005)
* Nagai Shrine karamon (designated June 14, 2005)
* 17 historical materials relating to Nagai Naokiyo (deposited at Takatsuki Castle Site History Museum)

== Nearby ==
* Catholic Takatsuki Church
* Japan Claretian Missionaries headquarters monastery

* Ruins of Takatsuki Castle and nearby historical park areas
